files.introductory_context:
# Checks: every "number to check" recomputed from the exported data

Written by `build/assemble/check_all.py`. The script reads only the files under `data/` and
`checks/expected.csv`; it recomputes each value with the file, filter and aggregation that `FIGURES.md` names
and compares it with the expected value. Run it again on any machine with python 3, pandas and numpy:

    python build/assemble/check_all.py

It ends with exit code 1 if a value differs.

- Checks: **1375**. Mismatches: **0**.
- Tolerance: 0.0001 for numbers (the expected values are stored with 4 decimals), 0 for counts, exact for text.
- `checks/expected.csv` was written by the same script (`--freeze`) on 2026-10-11 from the harmonised data, after
  the values had been compared with the builders' numbers, and frozen again after the final pass (what changed between
  the two is listed in `CHANGELOG.md` and in `checks/expected_changes_final_pass.csv`). The column "in builder text" says whether the value,
  rounded as printed, stands in the builder's own figure concept (`sections/<block>.md`), which that builder's
  script computed before the ids were harmonised: `yes` is an independent confirmation, `-` means the value is not
  printed there in this form (a count, a text value, an interval end, or a check added by the assembler).
- How each exported number compares with the SOURCE REPORTS on the server is in `checks/<block>.md`
  (written by the builders, who could read the reports; 0 unexplained differences).

# Data dictionary

One entry per file under `data/` (115 files). Written by `build/assemble/build_dictionary_md.py` on 2026-10-11 from the five
builders' dictionaries (`dictionary/<block>.md`), from the additions of the final pass (`dictionary/finalize.md`) and from the files
themselves: row counts and the lists of values are counted from the files as they are now, so they are true also after the ids and
names were harmonised and after the final pass. An entry that starts with "Changed in the final pass" or "Added in the final pass"
was changed after the builder wrote its text; where the two disagree, that first paragraph is right. An entry with a paragraph
"A8d refresh" was rebuilt, or deliberately left as it is, in the evening of 2026-10-11, when arm A8d of supp_prior_ablation was read
with three replicates (`dictionary/refresh_a8d.md`; `CHANGELOG.md`, section 8).
An entry with a paragraph "Operator-arm refresh" was rebuilt, or is new, on 2026-10-13, when the variance-only arm D1v2' of the
operator ablation had been scored (`dictionary/refresh_operator_arm.md`; `CHANGELOG.md`, section 10).

## How to read an entry

- **Rows**: counted from the file. **What one row is**, **how it was derived**, **server sources**, **intervals**: the builder's text.
  Server paths (`L/...`, `R/...`, `C/...` or relative paths) and their sha256 are provenance: they say where a number came from on the
  analysis server. Nothing in the export needs them. (`R` = the project root on the server, `L` = its improvement-loop folder, `C` = the
  prior campaign of 2026-10-09 inside `L`.)
- **Column table**: column, meaning and unit, and the values that occur in the file. For a column with at most 24 different text
  values (or 12 different numbers) all values are listed; otherwise the range or the number of distinct values. "empty in n of N rows"

# CellPFN paper: figure concepts and figure data (export of 2026-10-11)

For Philipp Flotho. Assembled by Claude on 2026-10-11 on the analysis server, from five blocks that were built in
parallel the same day, then verified twice (once from the export alone, once against the server sources) and corrected
in a final pass. What the verifications found, what was changed and what stays open: `CHANGELOG.md`.
Refreshed in the evening of the same day for one change on the server: arm A8d of the prior ablations was read with
three replicates (below, "What the A8d refresh did"; `CHANGELOG.md`, sections 8 and 9).
Refreshed again on 2026-10-13 for a second change on the server: the variance-only arm of the gene-gene operator ablation
(D1v2') was trained and scored, and fig6 now holds all three arms (below, "What the operator-arm refresh did";
`CHANGELOG.md`, section 10).

## What this is

A self-contained package for drawing the figures of the CellPFN paper on another machine:

- **the concept of every figure** (message, panels, which file with which filter gives each plotted value, the numbers a
  drawn figure must reproduce, caveats, open choices), and
- **all data needed to draw it**, as plain CSV files.

No figure is drawn and no image is in the package. Nothing in it needs access to the server.

Recompute every "number to check" of FIGURES.md from the exported data and compare it with checks/expected.csv.

    python build/assemble/check_all.py            # from the export root, or from anywhere

Reads ONLY files under data/ (relative to the export root) and checks/expected.csv. Needs python 3 with pandas and
numpy. Writes CHECKS.md and checks/recomputed.csv. Exit code 1 if a value differs from its expected value by more
than its tolerance, if an expected id is not computed, or if a computed id has no expected value.

Each check is computed exactly as the "Data" lines of FIGURES.md describe (file, filter, aggregation), so a check
that passes also shows that the filter in the text gives the number in the text.

Harmonise ids and vocabularies across the five builders' data files.

Run from anywhere:  python build/assemble/harmonize.py --stage ids
                    python build/assemble/harmonize.py --stage labels   (needs data/glossary__models.csv)

Reads and writes only files under <export root>/data. Every changed cell value is recorded in
build/assemble/renames.csv (file, column, old value, new value, number of rows, rule, reason).
The script is idempotent: a second run changes nothing and leaves the record as it is.

Stage "ids"    : model ids, panel ids, metric names, units, gene-view names, draw indices, label-set names.
Stage "labels" : sets model_label and family to the one canonical value per model_id of data/glossary__models.csv.

Only cell VALUES are changed. No column is renamed, added or removed, no row is added or removed, and no number
is touched.

Merge this run's renames into the record. An entry is keyed by (stage, file, column, old value, new value,
rule); an entry of this run replaces the stored entry with the same key, all other stored entries stay. So a
re-run after one builder regenerated its files refreshes that builder's entries and keeps the rest.

code_inspection.docstring:
Leak and hygiene scan over the whole export folder. Writes checks/hygiene_scan.md and exits 1 on a hard finding.

Hard findings (exit 1): a file above 20 MB; the export above 150 MB; a file type that must not be in the export
(arrays, pickles, checkpoints, images, archives, spreadsheets); a column or a value that looks like a ROSMAP donor,
specimen or cell identifier; a secret-like string; a gene-indexed or donor-indexed ROSMAP table; a ROSMAP row with an
age unit; an absolute path of the analysis server inside a data file.
Everything else is listed for the reader (where the word ROSMAP occurs, where "token" occurs and why it is harmless,
where absolute server paths occur in the documents and scripts).

code_inspection.docstring:
Build the fig4 data files of paper_export_20261011 (benchmark across support sizes).

Reads stored result tables only (no model is run, no number is typed by hand) and writes into X/data:
  fig4__cases.csv            long: one row per series x case x metric
  fig4__cases_wide.csv       convenience copy: one row per series x case, metrics as columns
  fig4__cells.csv            cell means as stored in the source reports + status rows (limit / not_run)
  fig4__panels.csv           facts per panel (classes, cells, genes, values, CellPFN input mode)
  fig4__methods.csv          what each series is (classifier, input, budget, caveat keys)
  fig4__caveats.csv          the caveats of the source reports, verbatim, keyed
  fig4__best_per_family.csv  the model TABLE_best.md shows per family, with the candidates it was chosen from
  fig4__table_best_cases.csv per-case values behind every row of gene_view_table_20261008/TABLE.md / TABLE_best.md
  fig4__scanvi_training_budget.csv, fig4__posthoc_diagnostics_cases.csv, fig4__posthoc_diagnostics_summary.csv
and X/sections/benchmark__models.csv, X/build/benchmark/sources_fig4.csv, build_fig4.log.json.

ROSMAP rows are dropped at the first read. Zebra-sex (one case, a different task) is not part of fig4.

Build the supp_exposure data files of paper_export_20261011 from EXPOSURE_REPORT.md (2026-10-08).

Every entry is parsed from the report text by this script; nothing is added. Files written into X/data:
  supp_exposure__study_exposure.csv   study x corpus (CELLxGENE Discover, scGPT whole-human, Geneformer-V2): the
                                      report's verdict, verbatim, with a 4-level class derived from its first words
  supp_exposure__panel_chances.csv    section 2 of the report: chance that the exact cells were seen, per panel x model
  supp_exposure__domain_shares.csv    tissue share of each pretraining corpus, as quoted in section 1
  supp_exposure__figure_marks.csv     the mark (* / (*) / none) per model x panel used in the tables and figures
The report's ROSMAP rows are bibliographic (which public study is in which public corpus); they hold nothing read
from the controlled-access stores, which this script never opens.

# Checks: benchmark block (fig4, supp_exposure)

Written by `build/benchmark/check_benchmark.py`. Column "recomputed" is computed from the exported files in `data/` only; column "source" is the value printed in the named report on the server; "diff" = recomputed minus source. A printed value has one decimal, so a difference up to 0.05 is rounding ("tol"); a printed difference of two one-decimal values can be off by 0.1 (group C). Every row is in `checks/benchmark__checks.csv`.

| A. TABLE_best.md | 293 | 293 | 0.05 |

| E. cell means | 3 | 3 | 6.667e-07 |
| F. ANSWER.md Table 1 (Zebra a / b / c) | 36 | 36 | 0.04994 |
| all | 668 | 668 | 0.08647 |

code_inspection.docstring:
A8d refresh (2026-10-11, after the A8 read-out of 19:39 UTC): compare the expected values frozen for the refresh
(checks/expected.csv) with the freeze after the final pass (checks/expected_before_a8d_refresh.csv).

Writes checks/expected_changes_a8d_refresh.csv: every check whose expected value changed, was added or was removed.
Exit code 1 unless exactly the intended changes are found: the three A8d values of supp_prior_ablation changed, ids
`refresh_a8d.*` were added, nothing was removed, and every other row of the two files is identical (id, figure, kind,
expected value, tolerance and the text that says how it is recomputed). Reads checks/ only; needs no server path.

    python build/finalize/expected_changes_a8d_refresh.py                # as in build/assemble/run_all.sh
    python build/finalize/expected_changes_a8d_refresh.py --report-only  # writes the same file, always exit code 0

After a LATER freeze of checks/expected.csv (another new read-out) the last record of this chain stops, because each

fig7: take ROSMAP out of the real reference (server only; run after build/method_realism_misc/build_fig7.py).

Why: ROSMAP is controlled-access data and the export leaves the server. The fig7 files as the builder wrote them held
(i) 84 + 40 rows of ROSMAP summary statistics (fig7__real_by_dataset.csv, fig7__real_by_study.csv) and (ii) pooled
real minima and maxima in fig7__sim_vs_real_summary.csv that are values of single ROSMAP units. The export rule
allows only aggregate performance values of ROSMAP (supp_rosmap). This script removes both.

What it does
  1. fig7__real_by_dataset.csv, fig7__real_by_study.csv: the rows with dataset == ROSMAP are dropped.
  2. fig7__sim_vs_real_summary.csv: every real-side column and every column derived from it is recomputed from the
     real units of the PUBLIC datasets only (PBMC, Zebra, kidney), with the rule of the realism judgment unchanged
     (judge/judge_analysis.py, functions verdicts() and verdict()). The verdict stored in the source report, whose
     real reference included ROSMAP for the "single" and "K8_32" references, is kept as a label in
     verdict_source_report. Before anything is changed the script recomputes every stored row WITH ROSMAP and
     stops unless it reproduces the stored table (real median, minimum, maximum, per-draw envelope, tail shares,
     percentile, coverage, both verdicts): so the only difference to the report is the removal of the ROSMAP units.
  3. fig7__class_granularity.csv: the pooled real groups are recomputed without the ROSMAP contrasts (same check).
  4. fig7__statistics.csv: real_n_units is the number of public units; the report's number is kept beside it.

No ROSMAP value is written or printed: ROSMAP rows of the reference tables are used only for the reproduction check
in memory. Reads the stored tables of the realism judgment (no ROSMAP data store is opened). Idempotent.

files.introductory_context:
# build/knockout - how the fig5 files were made

Run order (Python: `/local/landmark_project/conda/envs/hashprompt-loop-main-20260715/bin/python`, CPU only,
`PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`; about one minute in total):

1. `build_fig5.py` - reads the server sources (read-only) and writes every `data/fig5__*.csv`, plus
   `sources_sha256.csv`, `exported_files.csv`, `build_constants.json`, `server_check_noop_vs_expression.csv`.
2. `check_fig5.py` - reads only `data/fig5__*.csv`; recomputes the headline numbers and writes `checks/knockout.md`
   and `check_results.csv`. Runs on any machine (`python check_fig5.py <export root>`).
3. `verify_against_source_tables.py` - server only; compares the re-derived tables with the report's own aggregate
   tables and appends a section to `checks/knockout.md` (`server_verification.csv`).
4. `write_dictionary.py` - writes `dictionary/knockout.md` (fails if a column has no description).
5. `write_section.py` - writes `sections/knockout.md` and `sections/knockout__models.csv`; all numbers in the text are
   computed from the exported files.

No ROSMAP file is opened by any of these scripts. No expression matrix, checkpoint or token is written.

Rows: 12,600. Columns: 23. Size: 3.94 MB.

fig2 main table. One row per model x gene view x panel x support size x support draw x metric (the "case" level). 14 models: 7 tabular models (draws 0-2; `hvg2000`, `hvg8192`, `all`), 3 CellPFN states (draws 0-19; the same views plus `rand2000`, `rand8192`), Geneformer and scGPT with two classifiers each (draws 0-2; `own_input`). BA and NLL for every model, ECE15 for CellPFN.

- Sources: `diag1d_cases`, `diag1b_cases`, `realcell_cases`, `realcell_methods`.
- How derived: Tabular rows: `diag_1d .../tables/cases_long.csv` (its 2,000-gene rows are the stored benchmark cases, its wider views were scored in diagnostic 1d); `balanced_accuracy` x 100, `nll`; `status` `limit` with `limit_kind` `library_error` becomes `refused` with the message kept. CellPFN rows: `diag_1b .../tables/cases.csv` (all 20 draws, five views); the copy of G1v2' in the diag 1d table was checked to be identical (108 cases) and not duplicated. Geneformer / scGPT rows: `realcell_baselines .../new_cases_long.csv` (`ba_primary`, `nll`), panels PBMC and Zebra processed. `n_classes`, `n_query` and `label_set` are derived from the same tables. Nothing is recomputed from predictions.
- Legitimate intervals: Over support draws within one model x view x panel x support size: 20 draws for CellPFN, 3 for the others. Differences between views are paired by draw (same support cells, same query cells). Never pool over panels or support sizes for an interval. One training seed: no interval covers it.

gene_view.meaning_and_unit: Genes given to the model, chosen on the support cells of the case: `hvg2000`, `hvg8192`, `all`, `rand2000`, `rand8192`, `own_input` (Geneformer / scGPT); in `fig3__cases_other_views.csv`: `pca100` (at most 100 principal components fitted on the support cells), `mv72` (72-feature input of the July run).

n_genes.meaning_and_unit: Number of gene columns actually given to the model in this case (count). Empty where the source table does not store it (kidney and reconstructed-count Zebra in the 2,000-gene view; Geneformer / scGPT, which take a per-cell selection).

files.unit_of_analysis: fig2 main table. One row per model x gene view x panel x support size x support draw x metric (the "case" level). 14 models: 7 tabular models (draws 0-2; `hvg2000`, `hvg8192`, `all`), 3 CellPFN states (draws 0-19; the same views plus `rand2000`, `rand8192`), Geneformer and scGPT with two classifiers each (draws 0-2; `own_input`). BA and NLL for every model, ECE15 for CellPFN.
files.aggregation: Tabular rows: `diag_1d .../tables/cases_long.csv` (its 2,000-gene rows are the stored benchmark cases, its wider views were scored in diagnostic 1d); `balanced_accuracy` x 100, `nll`; `status` `limit` with `limit_kind` `library_error` becomes `refused` with the message kept. CellPFN rows: `diag_1b .../tables/cases.csv` (all 20 draws, five views); the copy of G1v2' in the diag 1d table was checked to be identical (108 cases) and not duplicated. Geneformer / scGPT rows: `realcell_baselines .../new_cases_long.csv` (`ba_primary`, `nll`), panels PBMC and Zebra processed. `n_classes`, `n_query` and `label_set` are derived from the same tables. Nothing is recomputed from predictions.
files.interval_definition: Over support draws within one model x view x panel x support size: 20 draws for CellPFN, 3 for the others. files.aggregation: BA and NLL are copied from the step-6 case table (ROSMAP and Zebra-sex rows dropped at the first read) and from the real-cell case table (`ba_primary`, `ba_cell`, `nll`, `mean_confidence`). ECE15 and macro-F1 are not in those two tables; they are read from the score table the step-6 row points to (`source_file`, `source_key`) for the same case, and kept only if the BA stored beside them equals the step-6 BA to 1e-6 (2,754 cases joined, 0 mismatches). macro-F1 is stored as a fraction in one table and in percent in another; it is exported in percent points. No ECE15 / macro-F1 is exported for kidney pt_sex (cell or donor level is ambiguous in the stores), for rows whose scores live only in per-case JSON files (July checkpoints, CellTypist, prototype and LDA rules) and for the real-cell round except scGPT LR (ECE15 from its track file).
files.interval_definition: Three support draws per PBMC/Zebra condition are descriptive points/ranges; kidney draws are donor-held-out folds. Do not infer uncertainty across heterogeneous panels or models (DATA_DICTIONARY.md: Which intervals are legitimate).

readiness.reason: Follow row-level status and dictionary interval rules; present estimates only for evaluated cells and maintain model/input restrictions.

values: All results are single training seed and descriptive. A cell is the mean over the 3 frozen support draws (kidney: 3 donor-held-out folds).

Both foundation models were very likely pretrained (without labels) on the exact PBMC cells; Geneformer-V2 also on the kidney cells and on the studies behind about 93% of the Zebra OOD query cells and at most 22% of the Zebra dev query cells; scGPT on no kidney and no Zebra query cell. Exposure was assessed only for scGPT and Geneformer. The percentages are a judgment from the evidence chain, not measurements.

Cells with more than 4,094 vocabulary genes are truncated to their top-ranked 4,094 (PBMC 179, Zebra 1,197, Zebra counts 1,040 cells). Zebra processed: tokens from expm1 of the supplied log1p CP10k. NCM cosine centroids are not centred.

Classifier differs from Geneformer's: scGPT's logistic regression is sklearn defaults (C=1) on the unit-length 512-d CLS embedding without standardisation; Geneformer's uses the benchmark's fit_logistic_reference (support-only standardisation, C=1). The scGPT LR probabilities are flat, most of all at small support, so its NLL is not comparable with other rows. Mean top-class probability on the query cells (from the stored probabilities), mean over a panel's cases: scGPT LR pbmc 0.24, kidney 0.62, zebra 0.37, zebra_counts 0.37; Geneformer LR (mean) pbmc 0.86, kidney 0.96, zebra 0.83, zebra_counts 0.85; scANVI inductive pbmc 0.27, kidney 0.60, zebra_counts 0.35; at PBMC l1 B1 the scGPT LR NLL is 2.00 against ln 8 = 2.08 for a uniform guess. Its BA also depends on the classifier, not only its NLL: refitting the Geneformer track's support-standardised LR on the stored scGPT embeddings (post hoc verifier diagnostic, not a result row) gives panel means of BA, declared -> diagnostic: PBMC 69.5 -> 73.5 (l1 B1 64.9 -> 61.2, l1 B10 77.5 -> 82.9, l1 B100 80.7 -> 88.0, l2 B1 55.7 -> 55.3, l2 B10 65.9 -> 71.5, l2 B100 72.0 -> 82.1), kidney 94.6 -> 96.2, Zebra 69.3 -> 68.6, Zebra counts 71.2 -> 69.9; per column -3.6 to +10.1 points. G1v2′ 12K minus the diagnostic (raw-count input, log1p CP10k input in brackets): PBMC +2.3 instead of +6.4, kidney +0.5 (-0.8) instead of +2.1 (+0.8), Zebra +1.5 instead of +0.8, Zebra counts +2.1 (+1.1) instead of +0.9 (-0.1). The NCM rows fit no weights and are the classifier-independent comparison of the two embeddings.

Input views differ. CellPFN, the prototype rules, CellTypist and the full-gene-panel LDA rows see the full gene panel of the dataset. The tabular models (TabICLv2 and its fine-tunes, TabPFN-3.5, Kumo Tabular and its fine-tunes), logistic regression and the HVG LDA rows see a support-only view of at most 2,000 highly variable genes (HVG-2000, log1p CP10k, genes chosen on the labelled support cells), or at most 100 principal components of it (PCA<=100). A difference between a CellPFN row and a tabular row therefore mixes model and input view.

Kidney: core5 and core9 are cell-level BA. pt_sex and pt_age are donor-level BA (one vote per query donor). The NLL of a pt_sex / pt_age cell is the cell-level NLL of the same predictions, because that is the only NLL stored with a kidney case. The B200 / B400 and pt_age cells exist only for GS1, GH1, GH1C and for C1v2p / G1v2p at 12K.

NCM and the LDA rules were computed at B10 and B100 only (a pooled within-class covariance is undefined with one cell per class) and store BA only. The kidney evaluation stores no NLL for the prototype rules. The NLL of prototype rules can be very large: these rules produce uncalibrated scores, and their NLL is shown as stored.

No probabilities (no NLL). Kidney pt_sex donor BA applies the benchmark's mean-per-donor rule to SingleR's correlation scores (before fine-tuning); a majority vote of the assigned labels gives 66.7 / 75.0 instead of 70.8 / 70.8 (panels A / B). Normalisation is a Python re-implementation of the logNormCounts formula. Markers: both rows used the default de.method 'classic' (markers from differences of label medians). The vignette of the installed SingleR 2.12.0 recommends de.method 'wilcox' for single-cell references, because the default 'may fail for low-coverage data where the median is frequently zero' (SingleR.Rmd lines 119-125). A post hoc verifier diagnostic with an approximation of the wilcox markers (top 10 Mann-Whitney AUC genes per label pair, then BiocPy SingleR unchanged; not a result row) gives panel means of BA, declared -> diagnostic: PBMC 69.8 -> 71.4, kidney 93.3 -> 94.5, Zebra 67.1 -> 67.5, Zebra counts 68.3 -> 68.8; per column -3.3 to +5.6 points. G1v2′ 12K minus the diagnostic (raw-count input, log1p CP10k input in brackets): PBMC +4.5 instead of +6.0, kidney +2.2 (+0.9) instead of +3.3 (+2.1), Zebra +2.6 instead of +3.0, Zebra counts +3.2 (+2.2) instead of +3.7 (+2.7). The declared rows stay as run (DESIGN.md: default settings).

One run per case (one training seed for scANVI; deterministic frozen embeddings for scGPT and Geneformer), 3 support draws or donor folds per cell, no intervals: descriptive only. About 1.5 BA points is within the spread of the support draws (step-6 rule of thumb).

Pre-registered scvi-tools defaults, fixed before any result and not retuned: scVI 400 epochs, then scANVI 10 epochs (about 10-20 optimizer steps at B1/B10: 10 x ceil(training cells / 128)); train_size 0.9 holds out 10% of the labelled support cells, rounded in favour of training (none of 4 or 8 cells at B1; 2 of 20 at PBMC l2 B1). At B1 and B10 the classifier is near-uniform: mean top-class probability on the query cells (range over the 3 draws): PBMC l1 B1 0.152-0.160 and l1 B10 0.172-0.186 (uniform 0.125); l2 B1 0.064-0.068 and l2 B10 0.090-0.098 (uniform 0.050); Zebra counts B1 and B10 0.271-0.312 (uniform 0.250). NLL at PBMC l1 B1 2.02 against ln 8 = 2.08 for a uniform guess. At PBMC l2 B1 only 18 of the 20 labelled cells enter scANVI training (train_size 0.9), so at least 2 classes have no training cell; at PBMC l1 B1 it predicts 4 to 5 of 8 classes (per draw 4, 5, 5). The B1/B10 BA and NLL of this row, and every G1v2′-minus-scANVI-inductive gap at B1/B10, therefore measure this training budget, not what scANVI can do with these labels. A frozen small-data scANVI recipe already exists in the project (`annotation_references_20260921/PROTOCOL.md`, scANVI section: scvi-tools 1.4.2, inductive, scVI 400 + scANVI 100 epochs, n_samples_per_label 100, all support rows in training), run on the 6 kidney panel-A B100 cases only. On the same cases it gives core5 A 96.3 and core9 A 97.7, against 94.5 and 97.7 for this row (section 5). This comparison is not a clean measure of the budget: it differs from this round's scANVI in scANVI epochs (100 vs 10; n_samples_per_label 100 vs none), genes (all 4,096 panel-A genes vs HVG-2000), likelihood (NB vs ZINB), depth (2 vs 1 layers) and hold-out (all support rows in training vs train_size 0.9). Sources: its six `run_manifest.json` files (6 of 6 agree) and `annotation_references_20260921/PROTOCOL.md` (scANVI section: 'all support rows in training, no validation selection/early stopping'); this round's per-case records of both variants (`results/scanvi_{inductive,transductive}/kidney/*.json`, 36 of 36 agree).
Pretraining-corpus overlap with these cells (CELLxGENE kidney, GEO PBMC, the cortex atlas studies) was not checked; any overlap is unlabelled (self-supervised) exposure.

REALCELL_REPORT.md section 5 still says that pretraining overlap on kidney "was not checked" and that CELLxGENE feeds scGPT's corpus. The later EXPOSURE_REPORT.md checked it: scGPT did not see the kidney cells (added to CELLxGENE 2024-06-14, after its corpus), Geneformer almost certainly did (via GEO). Use the exposure report.

Since the sign-off of 2026-10-02, real-data results are abort criteria only and tune nothing; earlier choices (operator family, primary cells, NLL and ECE15 as hard guards) were made with real-panel labels or results in view. The pre-registered gene-gene verdict at 12K was NOT SUPPORTED (N3: harm on the primary cell PBMC l1 B10).

TABLE_best.md shows one variant per family, chosen by the 2k-HVG mean on the reported panels (G1v2p as "our best", the LR classifier for Geneformer and scGPT). Choosing the best row per family on the reported panels is a selection on the evaluation data; the caption must state it.
TabPFN results are for non-commercial research use.
The G1v2' 12K control rows are the same weights with an intervention at inference (operator off; operator rank 0; support labels permuted; support genes shuffled). They are controls, not models.

The choice between Zebra reconstructed counts and processed values as the primary Zebra panel of the final evaluation is open (recommendation: reconstructed counts, on validity grounds). The gain of CellPFN on the counts panel is narrow (dev B1, about 10 BA) and comes mostly from the gene set; "count mode is better" is not supported.
Three draws per cell: B1 cells carry about +-5 points of draw noise. A BA difference under about 1.5 points is within the spread of the support draws (step-6 rule of thumb).

Uses the case's unlabelled query cells for training (donor batch key for cell-type cases), so it is not under the same protocol as the inductive rows; kept as the method's typical use. It ran the same pre-registered recipe as the inductive row (scVI 400 + scANVI 10 epochs, train_size 0.9). It is not near-uniform at B1 and B10: mean top-class probability on the query cells (range over the 3 draws) PBMC l1 0.226-0.308 (uniform 0.125), l2 0.203-0.386 (uniform 0.050); Zebra counts 0.632-0.792 (uniform 0.250). On Zebra counts its NLL at B1 and B10 is above ln 4 = 1.39 in 3 of 4 columns (1.64-1.99; ood B10 1.20), so there it is confident and often wrong. It trains on the support cells plus the unlabelled query cells: 296-900 cells per PBMC case and 6,451-7,029 per Zebra-counts case at B1 and B10, against 4-180 for the inductive row. Its 10 scANVI epochs are therefore about 30-550 optimizer steps, against 10-20 for the inductive row (10 x ceil(cells / 128)). Whether the budget limits this row was not measured. Its B1/B10 values, and the G1v2′-minus-scANVI-transductive gaps there, are what this pre-registered recipe gives; they are not a measure of the budget.
Zebra processed is a limit (no counts; scVI/scANVI model raw counts). Single seed, not re-run.

flash-attn not installed: embeddings come from scGPT's documented PyTorch encoder path (fp16 autocast); the distance to the flash-attention path the checkpoint was trained with was not measured. torch is pinned to 2.3.0 by torchtext 0.18.0. Cells with more than 1,199 expressed vocabulary genes are subsampled (documented default, seeded; 86% of PBMC cells).

class_label.meaning_and_unit: Class of the explained cell = its true and predicted class (only correctly called cells are explained). Short labels; full names in fig5__classes.csv. 'ALL' = all explained cells of the case pooled (only in the aggregate tables).

cell.meaning_and_unit: Row index of the cell in the query set of the case (0-based, benchmark order). Not a barcode; identifies a cell only within (case_id). The same cell can be explained under both models.

gene.meaning_and_unit: Gene symbol of the column (public panels). CellPFN never sees this name: it receives anonymous, permuted columns; names come from the case's column-to-symbol map.

gene_set.meaning_and_unit: Why the gene is in the exact-knockout set: top (in the class top-20 of at least one of gradient x input, IG, operator readouts), low (in the bottom-20 of IG or of the operator KO readout), top+low (both, for different methods), random (one of ~20 random genes expressed in at least one explained cell of the class), dsloo_extra (DS-LOO's own top-20 / bottom-20, knocked out afterwards). The report's faithfulness numbers use every set except dsloo_extra.

in_sq_subset.meaning_and_unit: 1 if the gene also has an exact support+query knockout (then exact_ko_sq_margin and dsloo_sq_margin are filled), else 0 and those two cells are empty (not run).

expr_dir.meaning_and_unit: Expression direction of the gene, given SEPARATELY from importance: hi / lo / eq = mean log1p-CP10k expression in the class's support cells is higher / lower / equal compared with the runner-up classes' support cells (weighted by how often each class is the runner-up of this class's explained cells). Same information as expr_direction in fig5__ko_pairs_by_class.csv.

exact_ko_margin.meaning_and_unit: GROUND TRUTH. Exact single-gene knockout effect on the margin: margin(cell) - margin(cell with this gene's query value set to 0), margin = logit(predicted class) - logit(runner-up class), fp32, logit units; the support is unchanged and the model recomputes its own depth and detected fraction. Positive = removing the gene lowers the margin (the gene's presence supports the call). Negative = removing it raises the margin. About 0 (/value/ <= 1e-4) = the gene is not expressed in this cell (knockout is a no-op) or has no effect.

dsloo_corr_margin.meaning_and_unit: DS-LOO + depth/detection correction: the fast estimate of exact_ko_margin, same sign convention and unit. This is the method of fig5.

dsloo_lin_margin.meaning_and_unit: DS-LOO linearised, before the depth/detection correction (same convention).

exact_ko_sq_margin.meaning_and_unit: Exact effect when the gene is set to 0 in the support cells AND the query cell, with a support refit (a different question); empty unless in_sq_subset = 1.

Rows: 600. Columns: 23. Size: 0.28 MB.

**Operator-arm refresh: rebuilt.** Two contrasts were added, 120 rows each (60 cells x 2 metrics): `cellpfn_d1v2p minus
cellpfn_c1v2p` (variance-only minus none: what per-gene variance whitening and its consumers add as a bundle) and
`cellpfn_g1v2p minus cellpfn_d1v2p` (full minus variance-only: what the covariance, low-rank term adds when the network is
trained with it). The existing rows (full minus none, and the two contrasts against R10K) are unchanged. 600 rows now. The
new rows were also computed by the scoring chain; the two computations agree to 1e-9 (`build/ablations/build_operator.py`
stops otherwise).

- Figure: fig6
- One row is: one row per contrast x panel x support size x gene view x metric
- Legitimate spread / intervals: 95% t interval over the 20 paired support draws (already computed in the row)
- How the file was derived: computed in this export from the 20-draw cases: difference a minus b on the same draw, mean, sample SD, t interval with 19 degrees of freedom. Not printed in any source report; descriptive, no correction for the number of cells or views
- Note: POST HOC with respect to the pre-registered 3-draw test (fig6__operator_n3_test.csv)
- Built by: `build/ablations/build_operator.py`

dictionary.preamble:
Rows: 48. Columns: 29. Size: 0.02 MB.

**Operator-arm refresh: new file.** The frozen analysis plan's reading of the 8 cells at 10 and 100 cells per class, for
balanced accuracy and for NLL improvement, in the three gene views (all genes, 8,192 and 2,000 variable genes): the three
arm levels, the three contrasts with their 95% intervals over the 20 paired draws, the plan's threshold theta and label per
contrast, and the plan's sentence for the cell. 48 rows. The plan fixed cells, thresholds and sentences before any D1v2'
score existed; the labels and sentences are the plan's, not the export's. B1 cells and the random-gene views are not read
by the plan and are not in this file.

- Figure: fig6
- One row is: one row per metric (balanced_accuracy, nll_improvement) x gene view (all, hvg8192, hvg2000) x panel x support size (10 and 100): the arm levels, the three contrasts with intervals, theta, the plan's label per contrast and the plan's sentence for the cell
- Legitimate spread / intervals: 95% t interval over the 20 paired support draws, in the columns vn_lo / vn_hi, fv_lo / fv_hi, fn_lo / fn_hi; none covers the single training run of each arm
- How the file was derived: copied from tier1_readings.csv of the scoring chain (make_tables.py under the frozen plan ANALYSIS_PLAN_FROZEN.md, sha256 694abc79...); the arm levels are checked against the exported cases. Labels and sentences are the plan's, not the export's. nll_improvement = NLL of the second arm of a contrast minus NLL of the first (positive: the first arm has the lower NLL)
- Note: the B1 cells and the random-gene views are not read by the plan: they have no theta, label or sentence and are therefore not in this file (their contrasts are in fig6__operator_paired_by_view.csv)
- Built by: `build/ablations/build_operator.py`

gene_view.meaning_and_unit: genes the model sees: all (the full gene panel of the dataset; count in n_genes), hvg8192 / hvg2000 (most variable genes chosen on the support cells only), random8192 / random2000 (seeded per case); hvg2000 is the input view of the tabular models and of the Kumo proxy

panel.meaning_and_unit: evaluation panel id: pbmc_l1, pbmc_l2 (PBMC CITE-seq, RNA only), zebra_dev, zebra_ood (Zebra HUMAN cortex atlas, processed values), zebra_counts_dev / zebra_counts_ood (reconstructed counts), kidney_<label set>_<A|B|efast>, zebra_sex, zebra_<task> (E-fast tier C), synthetic_<control>

support_per_class.meaning_and_unit: labelled support cells per class given to the model (1, 10, 100; kidney secondary 200, 400)

ba_pct_none.meaning_and_unit: balanced accuracy (mean per-class recall) in percent points, 0-100; arm none (C1v2'), mean over the 20 draws of the cell

ba_pct_variance_only.meaning_and_unit: balanced accuracy (mean per-class recall) in percent points, 0-100; arm variance only (D1v2'), mean over the 20 draws of the cell

ba_pct_full.meaning_and_unit: balanced accuracy (mean per-class recall) in percent points, 0-100; arm full operator (G1v2'), mean over the 20 draws of the cell

nll_none.meaning_and_unit: negative log-likelihood of the true class in nats (lower is better); arm none, mean over the 20 draws

nll_variance_only.meaning_and_unit: negative log-likelihood of the true class in nats (lower is better); arm variance only, mean over the 20 draws

nll_full.meaning_and_unit: negative log-likelihood of the true class in nats (lower is better); arm full operator, mean over the 20 draws

variance_only_minus_none.meaning_and_unit: contrast variance-only minus none (D1v2' - C1v2'), mean of the 20 paired differences (balanced-accuracy points; for metric nll_improvement: nats, positive = variance-only has the lower NLL)

vn_lo.meaning_and_unit: lower end of the 95% t interval of variance_only_minus_none over the 20 paired draws

vn_theta.meaning_and_unit: the plan's threshold theta for this contrast and view (balanced-accuracy points or nats; built from the B1 cells, in which the operator is off, and from the noise terms named in the plan)

vn_label.meaning_and_unit: the plan's label for variance-only minus none (ANALYSIS_PLAN_FROZEN.md section 3): resolved positive / resolved negative = the 95% interval excludes zero and the absolute mean is at least theta; small = the interval excludes zero and the absolute mean is below theta; equivalent within theta = the whole interval lies inside (-theta, +theta); not resolved = everything else. 'small' and 'equivalent within theta' can both hold ('small; equivalent within theta')
vn_label.documented_values: `equivalent within theta`, `resolved negative`, `resolved positive`, `small`, `small; equivalent within theta`

full_minus_variance_only.meaning_and_unit: contrast full minus variance-only (G1v2' - D1v2'): what the covariance (low-rank) term adds when the network is trained with it; same units as variance_only_minus_none

fv_lo.meaning_and_unit: lower end of the 95% t interval of full_minus_variance_only

fv_theta.meaning_and_unit: the plan's threshold theta for full minus variance-only

fv_label.meaning_and_unit: the plan's label for full minus variance-only (vocabulary as vn_label)
fv_label.documented_values: `equivalent within theta`, `not resolved`, `resolved positive`, `small`, `small; equivalent within theta`

full_minus_none.meaning_and_unit: contrast full minus none (G1v2' - C1v2'), mean of the 20 paired differences; same units

fn_lo.meaning_and_unit: lower end of the 95% t interval of full_minus_none

fn_theta.meaning_and_unit: the plan's threshold theta for full minus none

fn_label.meaning_and_unit: the plan's label for full minus none (vocabulary as vn_label)
fn_label.documented_values: `equivalent within theta`, `not resolved`, `resolved positive`, `small`, `small; equivalent within theta`

plan_rows.meaning_and_unit: number of cells of the plan's sentence table that this row belongs to (8 per metric and gene view)

sentence.meaning_and_unit: the plan's sentence for the cell, chosen by the plan's rule from the three labels (for example 'the gain in this cell needs the gene-gene covariance term; within theta points variance whitening alone gives none'); written before any D1v2' score existed
sentence.documented_values: `both parts contribute; the two means are given, no share is computed`, `no separable effect`, `no separable effect; not decomposed at this resolution (full - none...`, `per-gene variance whitening gives a gain in this cell; the covarian...`, `the gain in this cell needs the gene-gene covariance term; within t...`, `the operator's gain in this cell is reproduced by per-gene variance...`, `variance whitening with its consumers costs accuracy in this cell; ...`

sentence_caveat.meaning_and_unit: caveat that the plan attaches to the sentence in this cell (empty when none)

note.meaning_and_unit: free-text remark on the row; in the Stage 1 files also a recorded deviation of the run from the design (a8d r43: trained with one invalid task skipped, on the owner's decision)
note.documented_values: `PBMC l1 B10 is the cell of the N3 trigger; nothing relabels the ver...`; empty in 42 of 48 rows

**Changed in the final pass: ROSMAP is taken out of the real reference.** ROSMAP is controlled-access data, and the export rule allows only aggregate performance values of ROSMAP (in `supp_rosmap`). The builder's file copied the real side from the stored verdict table of the realism judgment, whose "single" and "K8_32" references hold ROSMAP units; its pooled minimum and maximum were values of single ROSMAP units. `build/finalize/fig7_public_real_reference.py` recomputed every real-side column and every column derived from it from the real units of the public datasets only (PBMC, Zebra, kidney), with the rule of the judgment unchanged. Before it changed anything it recomputed all 360 stored rows with the ROSMAP units and reproduced the stored table exactly, so the only difference to the source report is the removal of the ROSMAP units. The "K8" and "multistudy" references never held a ROSMAP unit: those 120 rows are unchanged. In 240 rows the real side changed; in 23 of the 360 rows the verdict class (inside / too high / too low / too wide) differs from the report's: 3 of the 34 primary rows of prior v2.2-B, none of the primary rows of prior v1 (late curriculum). The remarks after the verdict word (tail share, coverage) differ in further rows. The report's own verdict is kept as a label in `verdict_source_report`. The sentence of the builder's text above that says the real side is copied from `verdicts_long.csv` holds for the "K8" and "multistudy" rows only.

values: Dropping the signed-covariance lane changes low-support accuracy by less than the noise band (mean +0.57; draws -0.19 / +0.74 / +1.16); no guard fails. No detectable effect either way.
Harder classes made low-support accuracy worse than the learnable-only base in all three draws (-1.52 / -1.05 / -1.54, mean -1.37); the Tier A guard G1 fails.

No effect on OOD accuracy beyond noise (+0.16 / -0.21 / +0.65, mean +0.20; band 1.54). The frozen rule labels it UNRESOLVED (signs disagree) and prescribes two extension replicates. They were NOT run: with these three values at most 2 of 5 could clear the band and KEEP needs 4 of 5, so KEEP is out of reach. This is a departure from the letter of the rule; the reviewer notes that the mechanical end label would be DROP.

ROUTING LABEL, NOT EVIDENCE: the frozen trust gate does not let the proxy decide donor-level and calibration metrics (tiers B and C NOT_TRUSTED), so this arm was not decided; its flat numbers neither support nor rule out the change. Adult-age AUC of a2a1 against a1age: +0.0083 / +0.0000 / +0.0000, mean +0.0028. In stage1/readout/TABLES.md this arm still reads 'HELD (not built; design 6.0 stop: no admissible person-level age reference)'; it was built and read out afterwards with a OneK1K person-level age reference (design F2, F5).

ROUTING LABEL, NOT EVIDENCE: the frozen trust gate does not let the proxy decide donor-level and calibration metrics (tiers B and C NOT_TRUSTED), so this arm was not decided; its flat numbers neither support nor rule out the change. Donor-task AUC against the control: -0.0008 / -0.0080 / -0.0133, mean -0.0074.

ROUTING LABEL, NOT EVIDENCE: the frozen trust gate does not let the proxy decide donor-level and calibration metrics (tiers B and C NOT_TRUSTED), so this arm was not decided; its flat numbers neither support nor rule out the change. Tier B NLL against LR, improvement-signed: +0.0110 / -0.0347 / -0.0325, mean -0.0188 (negative = calibration worse than LR). The applier adds: 'not testable on the proxy (no calibration loss to repair)'.

ROUTING LABEL, NOT EVIDENCE: the frozen trust gate does not let the proxy decide donor-level and calibration metrics (tiers B and C NOT_TRUSTED), so this arm was not decided; its flat numbers neither support nor rule out the change. Worse-sex donor AUC against A1: -0.0089 / -0.0089 / +0.0357, mean +0.0060.

Read with three replicates: -0.43 / +0.60 / +0.87, mean +0.35. The three draws disagree in sign and the mean is below the keep threshold 1.5 (band 0.86). Rule 7.3 gives UNRESOLVED; the two extension replicates were not run (short cut of the frozen rule: fewer than two of the three differences exceed the band, so 4 of 5 is out of reach). No guard failed. The gap between 'unmeasured genes stored as zeros' and 'unmeasured genes removed' did not shrink (-0.20 / +0.47 / -0.06, mean +0.07, band 0.62). The label is NOT_TESTABLE, not DROP: the proxy's measured headroom (1.257 points) is below the keep threshold (1.5), so the proxy could not have shown a repair of keep size. This is no evidence that per-study detection does or does not work. Replicate r43: trained with a deviation from design section 6: the recipe preflight listed 1 invalid task of 12,640; the trainer skipped it, so one update of 625 used 19 tasks instead of 20; trained on the owner's decision of 2026-10-11, taken after replicates r42 and r44 had been read (stage1/a8/A8D_R43_INVALID_TASK.md; A8_DECISIONS.json 'training_deviations', accepted preflight report sha256 5cc2d050772f).

The only change that helped: low-support accuracy is above the control in all three task draws (+1.63 / +1.62 / +2.61, mean +1.95 points; keep threshold met, every draw beyond the noise band). The gain sits almost entirely on the Zebra cells (see supp_prior_ablation__cell_means.csv).

Zebra low-support accuracy rose by +0.90 (+0.52 / +0.54 / +1.64), below the keep threshold 1.5, and the calibration guard G3 failed (Tier B NLL worse by 0.099 nats, limit 0.03). The intended mechanism did not show: the gap between 'unmeasured genes stored as zeros' and 'unmeasured genes removed' shrank by +0.07 points against a band of 0.62; measured headroom 1.26 points, below keep.

# Data dictionary: benchmark block (fig4, supp_exposure)

Written by `build/benchmark/write_docs.py`. `L` = `/share/runs/2026/30-03-phflot-hashprompt/hashprompt_improvement_loop`. The sha256 values are those of the server files at build time; the exported files do not depend on them. All files: CSV, UTF-8, comma, header row. ## Rules for intervals

- Legitimate: the 3 support draws of a cell (show points or range); paired differences between two series on identical cases (`panel`, `support_per_class`, `draw`).
- Kidney: the 3 draws are donor-held-out folds, so their spread mixes donors and folds.
- Not legitimate: anything over the query cells or donors of a case (not exported; not independent); treating the cells of different panels as replicates; training-seed variance (one seed per CellPFN model).
- No task-draw replicates exist in this block.

## Not in this block

- ROSMAP (controlled access): no score of any kind. Zebra-sex (one case, a different task) is left out.
- CellPFN GL1 (learnable-only training): not in the source tables of this block; see the fig6 block.
- Expression values, cell or donor identifiers, model weights, tokens.
- TabPFN-3.5 numbers are for non-commercial research use.

# Data dictionary: additions and corrections of the final pass (2026-10-11)

Written by hand in the final pass, after the two verifications of the export. `build/assemble/build_dictionary_md.py`
reads this file after the five builders' dictionaries: the note of an entry is put at the top of that file's entry in
`DATA_DICTIONARY.md`, and the columns listed here are added to (or replace) the builder's column descriptions. The
scripts that made the changes are under `build/finalize/`.

## `data/fig7__sim_vs_real_summary.csv`

**Changed in the final pass: ROSMAP is taken out of the real reference.** ROSMAP is controlled-access data, and the export rule allows only aggregate performance values of ROSMAP (in `supp_rosmap`). The builder's file copied the real side from the stored verdict table of the realism judgment, whose "single" and "K8_32" references hold ROSMAP units; its pooled minimum and maximum were values of single ROSMAP units. `build/finalize/fig7_public_real_reference.py` recomputed every real-side column and every column derived from it from the real units of the public datasets only (PBMC, Zebra, kidney), with the rule of the judgment unchanged. Before it changed anything it recomputed all 360 stored rows with the ROSMAP units and reproduced the stored table exactly, so the only difference to the source report is the removal of the ROSMAP units. The "K8" and "multistudy" references never held a ROSMAP unit: those 120 rows are unchanged. In 240 rows the real side changed; in 23 of the 360 rows the verdict class (inside / too high / too low / too wide) differs from the report's: 3 of the 34 primary rows of prior v2.2-B, none of the primary rows of prior v1 (late curriculum). The remarks after the verdict word (tail share, coverage) differ in further rows. The report's own verdict is kept as a label in `verdict_source_report`. The sentence of the builder's text above that says the real side is copied from `verdicts_long.csv` holds for the "K8" and "multistudy" rows only.

| column | meaning and unit |
|---|---|
| `real_reference_scope` | Which real units the real side of this row rests on: the public datasets only (ROSMAP units removed in the final pass), or the reference of the source report unchanged (it holds no ROSMAP unit). |
| `real_n_units` | Number of real units of the reference in this export (public datasets only). |
| `real_q50` | Median over the real units of the reference in this export (public datasets only). |
| `real_min` | Smallest real unit of the reference in this export (public datasets only). |
| `real_max` | Largest real unit of the reference in this export (public datasets only). |
| `real_draw_q05_min` | Lower end of the per-draw envelope of the real units (smallest 5% quantile over matched draws), public datasets only; empty where the reference stores no per-draw quantiles. |
| `real_draw_q95_max` | Upper end of the per-draw envelope (largest 95% quantile over matched draws), public datasets only. |

## Conventions that hold in every file

- **Sign of an importance value (final convention, exactly as stored on the server).** Every knockout-type value
  is `margin(unperturbed cell) - margin(cell with the gene removed)`, where `margin = logit(predicted class) -
  logit(runner-up class)`; `_logit` variants use `logit(predicted class)` alone. Unit: logit units of the fp32
  model. **Positive = the gene's presence supports the call** (removing it lowers the margin). **Negative = the
  gene's presence argues for the runner-up.** Zero = not expressed in that cell (zero-knockout is a no-op) or no
  effect. The source code computes `KO - base` internally and stores the negated value (`code/dsloo.py`, comment
  "store: dl is (KO - base); report base - KO"); the exact knockouts are stored as `base - KO` directly
  (`code/run_case.py`). Nothing was re-signed for this export. DS-LOO and exact knockout have the same sign on
  99.7 % or more of the entries that move by more than 1e-3 (checks).

# Figure concepts, block `ablations`

Covers **fig6** (what the model needs: gene-gene operator ablation and task mix), **supp_prior_ablation** (Stage 1
prior ablations on the proxy, forest plot) and **supp_taskmix_tradeoff** (learnable-only training: accuracy against
calibration, and the dependence on the gene view).

This file describes figures; it draws none. Every number below was computed by `build/ablations/build_sections.py`
from the files in `data/`. Column meanings, row counts, sources and legitimate intervals: `dictionary/ablations.md`.
Recomputation against the source reports: `checks/ablations.md`. Model ids: `sections/ablations__models.csv`.

Terms used below. *Support size* B1 / B10 / B100 = 1 / 10 / 100 labelled cells per class. *Cell* (of a table) = one
panel x support size. *Draw* = one random choice of the support cells; the query cells are fixed. *Zebra* is a HUMAN
cortex atlas built from several studies (Flotho et al.), not zebrafish; "dev" and "OOD" are two splits of it, OOD
with query donors from held-out studies. *Update* = one optimizer step on 4 simulated tasks.

All CellPFN results in this block come from **one training run per model (one seed)**. Intervals cover the choice
of support cells only.

# Block `method_realism_misc`: figure concepts for fig1, fig7 (candidate), supp_stored_zeros, supp_rosmap; shared glossary

Written by `build/method_realism_misc/build_sections.py` on 2026-10-11. Concepts and data only: no figure is drawn and no image is part of the export. Every number below is taken by script from the files under `data/`; `checks/method_realism_misc.md` sets the headline numbers beside the source reports. Server paths in `Source:` notes start at `R` = `/share/runs/2026/30-03-phflot-hashprompt`; they are provenance, the export does not depend on them. 'Zebra' is the Zebra **human** cortex atlas (Flotho et al.), not zebrafish.

Files of this block: `data/fig1__*.csv` (4), `data/fig7__*.csv` (6), `data/supp_stored_zeros__*.csv` (8), `data/supp_rosmap__*.csv` (2), `data/glossary__*.csv` (3); column meanings in `dictionary/method_realism_misc.md`.

---

## fig1 — Concept: a simulator prior, gene-anonymous episodes, in-context prediction on real cells

**Status: ready** (as a fact sheet; fig1 is a schematic and needs facts, not measurements). One thing can still change how the operator is drawn: its ablation (fig6) is done with one training run per arm, and its pre-registered test did not support it as a gain.

**Message in one sentence.** A network that has only ever been trained on simulated single-cell datasets classifies real cells from a handful of labelled examples in one forward pass, without knowing which gene is which.

### Panels

- **a — Simulator prior (schematic).** Show the hierarchy of one simulated dataset: studies (= batches) > donors > cell types > cells, with a hidden class tree, cell-state programs and donor metadata, and the count model at the end. One dataset = 8 donors x 8 cell types x 256 cells x 8,192 genes (integer counts). The reader should see that a dataset is generated from a random recipe, not from real expression profiles.
- **b — Episode (schematic).** From one simulated dataset: choose a task (cell type, donor group by a metadata variable, or donor identity), 2-8 classes, 1-100 labelled support cells per class and 100 query cells per class; then keep a random subset of the genes in random order (2,048, 4,096 or 8,192 columns). Draw the gene axis as unlabelled, shuffled columns that are the same columns in support and query. The reader should see: labels only on the support, no gene names anywhere.

# Figure concepts: fig2 (scaling to the full transcriptome) and fig3 (the simulated prior transfers)

Block `scaling_transfer` of `paper_export_20261011`. Concepts and data only: nothing is drawn here. Every result number
below was computed from the exported files by `build/scaling_transfer/check_scaling_transfer.py` and filled in by
`build/scaling_transfer/write_sections.py`; `checks/scaling_transfer.md` shows each of them next to the value in the
source report.

## Terms used in both figures

- **Case.** One model on one panel, one label set, one support size and one support draw. A case is one row group of the
  `*__cases.csv` files (one row per metric).
- **Result cell.** One panel x support size (for example PBMC l1 at 1 cell per class). Its value is the mean over the
  support draws of its cases. The four core panels x three support sizes give 12 result cells.
- **Panels.** `pbmc_l1` (8 cell-type classes, 320 query cells), `pbmc_l2` (20 classes,
  800 query cells), `zebra_dev` and `zebra_ood` (4 classes each; 7,769 and 7,163 query
  cells). "Zebra" is a HUMAN cortex atlas (Flotho et al.), not zebrafish; `dev` and `ood` are its development and
  out-of-distribution query sets, on the processed values as supplied. Query sets are fixed; only the support cells change
  between draws.
